claim: That's why the NATO Alliance was created to secure peace and stability in Europe after World War 2.
rationale: NATO was founded by the 1949 Washington Treaty, after WWII (ended 1945), as a collective-defense alliance to secure peace and stability in Europe.

claim: The only president ever to cut the deficit by more than one trillion dollars in a single year.
rationale: The ~$1.4T one-year deficit reduction is numerically accurate but multiple fact-checkers (PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, CRFB) rate the framing misleading: the deficit fell chiefly because pandemic emergency spending expired as planned, and Biden's own policies added to deficits.

claim: And with 75 percent of adult Americans fully vaccinated and hospitalizations down by 77 percent, most Americans can remove their masks, return to work, stay in the classroom, and move forward safely.
rationale: 75% of adults fully vaccinated matches CDC (75.1% of those 18+ as of Mar 9, 2022); COVID hospitalizations fell sharply from the Jan 2022 Omicron peak (~38.4 per 100k adults). The specific 77% decline is consistent with the sharp post-peak drop, though the exact figure was not independently pinned — hence med confidence.

claim: We shared with the world in advance what we knew Putin was planning and precisely how he would try to falsely justify his aggression.
rationale: The US publicly declassified intelligence weeks before the Feb 2022 invasion detailing Russia's plan to fabricate a false pretext (incl. a staged propaganda video) to justify aggression.

claim: Our economy grew at a rate of 5.7 percent last year, the strongest growth in nearly 40 years, the first step in bringing fundamental change to an economy that hasn’t worked for the working people of this nation for too long.
rationale: BEA data: US real GDP grew 5.7% in 2021, the largest annual growth in 37 years (since 1984) — consistent with 'nearly 40 years'.

claim: Now our infrastructure is ranked 13th in the world.
rationale: The 13th-place figure derives from the 2019 WEF Global Competitiveness Report's broad infrastructure-quality measure; the number is accurate as cited.
edge_case: the WEF measure is debated but the cited figure is accurate

claim: There’s been a law on the books for almost a century to make sure taxpayers’ dollars support American jobs and businesses.
rationale: The Buy American Act (1933) requires the federal government to prefer US-made products in its purchases; 'almost a century' (1933->2022, ~89 yrs) is accurate.

claim: Insulin costs about $10 a vial to make.
rationale: A BMJ Global Health study estimated production cost at $2.28-$3.42/vial (human) and $3.69-$6.16 (analog); '$10 a vial' overstates the best estimate, though it directionally supports the low-cost/high-price point.
edge_case: right order of magnitude but exceeds the study estimate

claim: And while we’re at it let Medicare negotiate lower prices for prescription drugs, like the VA already does.
rationale: As of the March 2022 speech, Medicare Part D's 'noninterference' clause barred price negotiation while the VA negotiates via a national formulary (paying ~54% less); Medicare negotiation authority came later via the Aug 2022 IRA.
edge_case: accurate as of the speech date; the law changed later in 2022

claim: The American Rescue Plan gave schools money to hire teachers and help students make up for lost learning.
rationale: ARP provided ~$122B in ESSER K-12 funds explicitly used to hire teachers/staff and address learning loss via tutoring and summer/after-school programs.

claim: All Democrats, every single one of them, voted against these really important and very necessary massive tax cuts.
rationale: The 2025 reconciliation tax law (H.R.1) passed on party lines; the official Senate roll call (Vote 372, final passage) records 0 Democratic Yea votes and all House Democrats voted no, so 'all Democrats voted against' holds.
edge_case: the bill also drew some Republican defections, but no Democrat voted yes

claim: And record-setting inflation that cost the typical family $34,000 in just a speck of time.
rationale: 'Record-setting' is false: inflation peaked at 9.1% CPI in 2022 (highest since 1981, not an all-time record). The '$34,000' cost figure is also inflated/unsupported (closest documented estimate ~$28,000). Real high-inflation kernel, distorting framing.
edge_case: the $34,000 figure is not sourced to any authoritative document

claim: Thomas Jefferson drew his last breath.
rationale: Thomas Jefferson died at Monticello on July 4, 1826 (age 83), the 50th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence and the same day as John Adams.

claim: One drug has been costing Catherine $4,000 to purchase.
rationale: A specific private individual's ('Catherine') drug purchase cost; no authoritative public source can confirm or refute a named person's private out-of-pocket price.
edge_case: private/individual anecdote — no authoritative source exists

claim: Both Dominican Americans who’d grown up on the same streets they later chose to patrol as police officers.
rationale: A private biographical detail about two named individuals (where they grew up / became officers); not adjudicable from any authoritative public source.
edge_case: private/individual anecdote — no authoritative source exists
